title: Green Society v. State of Punjab (Pollution)
text: A public interest writ petition under Article 226 challenges continued operation of an industrial unit discharging untreated effluents into a river. The petitioner, an NGO, seeks closure of the polluting unit. The court examines reports of the State Pollution Control Board which confirm persistent violations of effluent discharge standards. The right to a clean environment is a facet of the fundamental right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution. The High Court issues a writ of mandamus directing the Pollution Control Board to seal the polluting unit within 72 hours. The industrial unit shall not be allowed to resume operations until it installs certified effluent treatment plants. The court also imposes a fine of Rs 50,00,000 to be deposited with the Pollution Control Board for river restoration. The fundamental rights of citizens to a clean environment must be enforced.
